title: Large personal MSX, Acorn, GEM and media-tool discovery
summary: Personally screen 182 candidate URLs and add 30 projects, with three scope/implementation exclusions and one relocated-source access deferral.
notes: Root assistant performed all research and main publication without delegating to a worker or creating a PR/branch. Eleven searches spanned native GEM and datatype tools, C64 sprites, Apple media, MSX development and Acorn disassemblies. Unrelated micro:bit/business MSX search collisions were screened out. Every addition has actual implementation evidence, with original-source, maintenance, reverse-engineering-derived and general tooling scope distinguished. Deprecated Apple converters, partial emulator timing, FPGA-only utilities, native-versus-host editors and incomplete format claims remain qualified. Only PIPELINE has explicit Claude authorship evidence in this reviewed batch; agent integration, a human named Claude and an AI sample image do not prove AI-written code. No upstream program, ROM, disk image, mapper probe, serial link or privileged installer was executed. The migrated mkcas site required a bot check and was not bypassed. Primary large/legacy-encoded files are linked immutably rather than silently altered into evidence.

sources.reason: Self-contained MOD replay library derived from 8bitbubsy behavior reconstructed from ProTracker disassembly; includes multichannel and MTM extensions.
CPC 464/664/6128 emulator combines access tracing, source generation, Vortex opcode/data decoding and sjasmplus byte comparisons.
Historical a2catalog and a2nibblize implementations generate catalogue/VTOC and nibble encodings, with 13/16-sector variants.
Parses Sider partitions and extracts, replaces, resizes or moves volumes, distinguishing 256-byte blocks from padded SCSI2SD captures.
Scripts inventory image hashes/boot sectors in SQLite and compare boot-code similarity, with simulation and graph helpers.
High-level AES forms, dialogs and window support with translated Doxygen documentation and original implementation.
Historical flying dialogs, window/forms and font-selection helpers include Atari and contributed PC GEM paths.
Grunenberg GEM toolkit adapted to modern MiNT GCC/GemLib, including event, dialog, window, clipboard and drag/drop support.
Small native display workbench separates bitmap, graphics, screen, input and window lifecycle handling.
Datatype parses Autodoc sections and marker decorations and formats documentation using native class methods.
Small native datatype-based image viewer demonstrates picture loading and Intuition display.
Native editor handles 64 sprites, multicolor/hires drawing, flood fill, animation and overlay previews, with PRG saving.
Windows editor separates sprite pools and eight-hardware-sprite frame composition, supports hires/multicolor and assembly/binary export.
wav2cas, cas2wav and casdir implement tape-audio decoding/encoding and block listings.
Native information/configuration panels and profiles communicate with OCM-PLD expanded I/O ports.
Forth libraries expose MSX BIOS/DOS, graphics and PSG operations, with text-to-block conversion and image-building scripts.
Preprocessor expands labels/constants, joins split statements and generates numbered BASIC lines; examples cover several vintage dialects.
Clusters animation tiles per MSX1 screen bank and emits tile/attribute/name-table assembly plus demo ROM source.
Modular converter supports labels, long variable names, macros and editor/build integration for classic BASIC outputs.
Windows editor manages mono/multicolor sprite collections and generates assembler, C and BASIC data; formatting implementation inspected.
Reconstructed PIC compression/decompression closely follows original Z80 behavior, preserving unusual fill/copy and row rules.
cptodsk writes host files into MSX disk images using FAT12 directory and cluster operations.
Host sender and native receiver use a framed CRC protocol over joystick-port software serial for cross-development transfers.
Kotlin image/resource library implements IMGX chunks, palettes, screen types, compression adapters and V9990 command chunks.
BIOS wrapper, sprite/pattern manager and Arkos AKM music/effect integration support Screen 2 game development.
Version-controlled rebuildable spreadsheet ROM source covers BBC, Master, Electron and Italian variants with explicit feature switches.
Partly commented reconstruction of the Electron Expansion 2.02 ROM, including joystick/OS integration and relocated thunks.
Annotated game, graphics/level editors, BASIC menu and hidden-sector loaders reconstruct the original disk structure including deleted-data marks.
Parses CAS markers and extracts ASCII, BASIC, binary and custom blocks with original addressing metadata.
Native mapper scan reports largest detected expansion and slot through explicit bank probing and BIOS output.
README-only statement of an intended Lua GEM binding; no implementation or distributed binding artifact is present.
Current default tree contains only license/attributes, with no dumping implementation or usage artifact to inspect.

Three-command CI installer only clones, builds and installs existing Cadius; no distinct media-format implementation or substantive analysis is present. Keep this as a convenience dependency rather than another disk-tool record.

GitHub is only a relocation notice to git.usebox.net/mkcas. The current upstream returned a bot-check page instead of source; inspect the author-hosted implementation through an authorized accessible route before qualifying current scope.
